title: Signal · Wednesday 28 October
overview: UBS beats its cost-saving goal and ties buybacks to the capital debate, Temenos raises its guidance, and Microsoft offers 60,000 staff voluntary departure.

top.headline: UBS lifts pre-tax profit 27% and raises its cost-saving goal to $13.7bn
top.summary: UBS reported third-quarter net profit of $2.69bn, up 8%, and pre-tax profit of $3.59bn, up 27%. Wealth management drew $55.1bn of net new assets. Savings from the Credit Suisse integration reached $13.2bn, and UBS now expects about $13.7bn by the end of 2026, above its earlier ambition of about $13.5bn.
top.background: Parliament is debating how much capital UBS must hold against its foreign subsidiaries; the proposal sits with a committee and is expected in the National Council in December, according to Reuters.
top.why: UBS has bought back $1.8bn of its $3bn programme and links the rest to that debate, so Parliament's decision now sets the pace of its shareholder returns. About 90% of the legacy Credit Suisse applications in scope are fully decommissioned, the bank said.
top.watch_next: The National Council's debate on the capital rules, expected in December.

top.headline: Temenos raises its 2026 profit guidance after a strong third quarter
top.summary: The Geneva banking software maker reported third-quarter revenue of $292.8m, up 13%, and non-IFRS EBIT of $109.3m, up 29%. Annual recurring revenue rose 12% in constant currency to $903.6m. Temenos now expects 2026 EBIT growth of about 12% and earnings per share growth of about 10%, up from about 9% and 7%.
top.background: Subscription and SaaS revenue rose 23% to $121.8m; one large deal in Africa slipped into the first days of the fourth quarter.
top.why: Temenos's results are a read on how much banks are spending to renew core banking, and its shift to subscriptions shapes what many Swiss and European banks pay for the platforms they run on.
top.watch_next: Whether the delayed African deal lifts fourth-quarter subscription revenue.

top.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary departure to about 60,000 staff as AI spending grows
top.summary: About 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of Microsoft's workforce, can leave with a severance payment, according to an internal memo reported by Business Insider and covered by ICTjournal. Windows, Xbox, Copilot and finance teams are included; some data centre, sales, security and quantum roles are not, Bloomberg reported.
top.background: Earlier this year Microsoft offered a similar programme to about 9,000 employees, and nearly a third accepted.
top.why: Bloomberg links the programme to AI infrastructure spending that is squeezing budgets and hiring elsewhere in the company, a trade-off that technology budgets at banks face as well.

items.headline: Deutsche Bank uses agentic AI to draft source-of-wealth assessments
items.summary: Inside its KYC platform, the private bank's tool extracts and reconciles client information and drafts a memo that staff check and approve. It is live for some income-related checks in Singapore and Hong Kong and is being extended to Europe, Yiping Li, global chief operating officer of the private bank, told WealthBriefing.
items.why: Source-of-wealth files are a slow, manual step in private banking onboarding; a live deployment with human sign-off gives Swiss banks weighing the same use a reference point.

items.headline: LGT moves AI from pilots to client processes, starting with contact logs
items.summary: An internally deployed tool now turns client conversations into draft contact logs that staff review and submit, said Simon Gomez, head of data and innovation at LGT Private Banking. The hardest part was getting colleagues to try it; demonstrations and peer feedback helped.
items.why: A private bank describing what adoption took, beyond a working pilot, is a practical benchmark for Swiss peers planning adviser tools.

items.headline: HSBC's third-quarter pre-tax profit rises 32% to $9.6bn
items.summary: Revenue rose 5% to $18.6bn, driven by banking net interest income, and HSBC plans a share buyback of up to $1bn. Much of the profit rise reflects $1.4bn of legal provisions a year earlier that did not recur, the bank said.
items.why: HSBC kept its target of a return on tangible equity of 17% or better through 2028; in Asian wealth management it is a direct competitor of the Swiss banks.

items.headline: Revolut will let retail clients invest in private tech companies from 2027
items.summary: Revolut Ventures, run with Carne Group as a European long-term investment fund (ELTIF), will offer positions in unlisted companies through the app, according to Fintech News Switzerland, citing Bloomberg. BNY will be custodian.
items.why: Private markets are reaching retail through apps, ground that Swiss private banks have kept for wealthy clients.

items.headline: Deutsche Börse opens DAX 40 shares to round-the-clock trading on 360X
items.summary: Outside Xetra hours, DAX 40 stocks now trade overnight and at weekends on the 360X venue through requests for quotes, settling into existing Clearstream accounts, according to Fintech News Switzerland.
items.why: Trading in large European stocks around the clock pushes banks' execution, risk and operations teams to cover hours they have not staffed.

items.headline: SAP lets its Joule agents run processes across SAP and other systems
items.summary: At TechEd in Berlin, SAP made Joule Work generally available: users state a goal and agents coordinate the applications and data needed, including third-party systems, with role-based permissions, audit logs and human checkpoints. An Enterprise AI Gateway follows in the first quarter of 2027.
items.why: Many banks run finance and HR on SAP; agents acting across systems with audit trails move governance questions from pilots to production.

items.headline: Salesforce adds a kill switch and hard spending limits for AI agents
items.summary: Agent Fabric gains evaluations that test agents before and during production and can trigger a kill switch, plus a FinOps dashboard with spending limits that block requests before budgets are exceeded. The kill switch and cost controls are available now; the evaluations enter beta in November.
items.why: Ways to stop a failing agent and cap its cost are what bank risk teams ask for before agents touch client processes.

items.headline: Anthropic reports early results from six drug development partnerships using Claude
items.summary: At Enveda, Claude reviewed 1,061 pages of manufacturing documents, found all 11 issues human reviewers had found plus seven more, and cut review time by 89%, Anthropic said. Partners include Bristol Myers Squibb and Generate Biomedicines; the work is early and mostly preclinical.
items.why: The document review result is the part that carries over: banks' compliance teams run similar checks on long regulated documents.

items.headline: 1Password lets AI agents sign in to services without seeing passwords
items.summary: With 1Password for Agents, an agent asks to log in, the user approves on their device, and 1Password fills in the credentials directly. It works with agents from Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI, according to Netzwoche.
items.why: How agents authenticate is among the first questions a bank's security team asks; approval for each login is one practical answer.

Swiss software survey: over 88% build with AI, 11.8% with orchestrated agents

say_it_today: UBS has taken $13.2bn of costs out of the Credit Suisse merger and switched off about 90% of the legacy applications in scope. The pace of its buybacks now rests on how much capital Parliament asks it to hold.
